evidence: Plaut. Poen. 405: Mox dabō, quom ab rē dīvīnā redierō
terms.comment: The everyday answer to “let’s do it!” when the answer is “not this minute”: it can stand alone (Mox.) or with a future (mox faciēmus). Sooner still is jam with a future (see in a moment); for a later time that is not near, posteā or posterius (see later).

terms.gloss: a little later, a little after
evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.5.2: mālō tē paulō post valentem quam statim imbēcillum vidēre
Cic. Brut. 229: hōc dē ōrātōre paulō post plūra dīcēmus
terms.comment: Literally “later by a little”, so it is measured from a point: in a story from the event just told, which is where it is most often met; in conversation from now, as when Cicero sets it against statim. It is good Latin for the future, but as an answer it wants something to lean on (prīmum cēnābimus, paulō post ignem faciēmus); the bare one-word reply is mox.

phrases.latin: Dā ergō, ut crēdam, sāvium. — Mox dabō, quom ab rē dīvīnā redierō.
phrases.english: Then give me a kiss, so that I believe it. — I will in a little while, when I’m back from the sacrifice.

phrases.latin: mālō tē paulō post valentem quam statim imbēcillum vidēre
phrases.english: I would rather see you a little later and well than at once and weak

phrases.latin: Ignem faciāmus! — Mox; prius cēnandum est.
phrases.english: Let’s make a fire! — In a little while; we have to have dinner first.
